conditions: Same $gst schema version (currently 1.0)
Same knowledge version as resolved at run time
Compatible with an established 8-phase tick cycle
falsificationCriteria: Two independent builds of the same seed produce different hashes
A canonical seed cannot be re-derived from its program output
Cross-language projection diverges from the canonical reference output
claims.scope: Within packages/canon-foundation and the supplied reference architectures only; does not yet include cross-language, end-to-end seed-to-artifact tests for arbitrary programs. [Prompt 2: Prompt 2: Gene Protocol implemented, seed-to-IR-to-plan pipeline skeleton built, entropy channels with golden vectors verified, constraint/capability/effect model distinct.]
claims.statement: The Core GSPL hypothesis is provisionally viable: supported by foundational implementation, not yet proven by end-to-end program reconstruction. Promotion to PROVEN requires seed-to-codebase reconstruction, deterministic recompilation, nontrivial architecture synthesis, behavioral equivalence, cross-language projection, test preservation, and reproducibility from independently repeated builds.
claims.verificationMethod: Run npm test in packages/canon-foundation; cross-check two independent seed expansions produce byte-identical canonical hashes (Prompts 2-3 deliver tests).

conditions: No special-purpose or lossy compression attempted.
falsificationCriteria: A constructive universal compressor is published with formal correctness proof
Kolmogorov-incompressible strings are shown to be compressible in practice
claims.scope: Universal; applies to all candidate compression schemes including any that GSPL might propose. Defended via Kolmogorov complexity (1965).
claims.statement: Universal arbitrary-data compression (one shorter description for every input) is REFUTED.
claims.verificationMethod: Cite Kolmogorov (1965) and standard textbooks on algorithmic information theory; no implementation necessary.

conditions: Both paradigms are Turing-complete
falsificationCriteria: A constructive proof of perfect translation between two paradigms is published
Two paradigms are shown to differ only in notation, not in semantics
claims.scope: Universal; applies to any candidate perfect-translation theorem between Turing-complete paradigms. The graduated-fidelity claim stands.
claims.statement: Perfect universal cross-paradigm translation is REFUTED. Translation between programming paradigms loses structural meaning because paradigms encode non-equivalent semantic invariants. GSPL supports GRADUATED translation fidelity (RC-1..RC-8) but not perfect translation.
claims.verificationMethod: Cite Felleisen (1991) on the expressive power of programming languages; argue structural non-equivalence of paradigms.

conditions: Seed in scope of canonical $gst schema
Knowledge version matches the interpreter build
No external state leaks
falsificationCriteria: Two runs of the same seed produce different outputs
The reconstructed program is observably different from the original
claims.scope: For seeds expanded by the canonical canon-foundation interpreter and codegen pipeline over a closed set of canonical gene types. [Prompt 2: Prompt 2: 5-layer pipeline (Authoring->Seed->IR->Plan->Artifact) implemented. Compiler context with resource limits. 3 reference fixtures (software architecture, interactive scene, mixed video/game) defined.]
claims.statement: Seed-first program reconstruction: given a GSPL seed, the canonical program it represents can be reconstructed (artefact and intermediate state both derivable from the seed).
claims.verificationMethod: Run the canonical interpreter twice with the same seed + knowledge version and assert output equivalence via SHA-256 (Prompt 2 delivers the test).

conditions: A seed uses the canonical combinator gene types
A canonical knowledge version is loaded
Targets are within the documented scope
falsificationCriteria: Two projections of the same seed against the same target do not produce equivalent artifacts
A combinator type fails the per-type property tests
claims.scope: Within the design contract of the 17 initial gene types; targets JavaScript and WGSL-class architectures. [Prompt 2: Prompt 2: Gene Protocol replaces fixed 17 with extensible registry. Multi-projection model supported through target contracts in seed dependencies. 3 reference fixtures span different target types.]
claims.statement: The Canonical multi-projection model allows a single seed to be projected into multiple target architectures through the `struct`, `graph`, `topology`, and `field` gene-combinator types. The mechanism is DESIGNED but not yet production-validated across architectures.
claims.verificationMethod: Build a 3-target projection test in Prompt 3: parse, lower, and hash against three independent Hash implementations.

conditions: Per-type property tests are exhaustive
Composition is closed under the 5-operator suite
No third-party gene extension is implicit
falsificationCriteria: A gene type T can be emulated by composition of other types
A counterexample gene-type removal is shown to be recoverable
claims.scope: Universe of canonical gene types as defined in spec/02; the claim is open to hostile review. [Prompt 2: Prompt 2: 17 types classified (12 CORE, 4 LIBRARY, 1 SECURITY). Irreducibility remains research-only; extensible protocol makes removal unnecessary.]
claims.statement: The initial 17-gene inventory is IRREDUCIBLE: removing any one of the 17 gene types loses expressiveness that cannot be recovered by composing the rest. This claim is empirically motivated in spec/02 but is NOT proven; it remains RESEARCH_REQUIRED.
claims.verificationMethod: Hotile review: identify a candidate gene type T and attempt to emulate it by composition of the other 16; if any composition reconstructs T, the claim is falsified.

conditions: Same $gst schema version
Same knowledge version
Same input seed
Identical determinism stack
falsificationCriteria: Two architectures produce different hashes for the same input
A non-canonical RNG introduces divergence
claims.scope: Architectures that implement the canon-foundation determinism stack without algorithmic substitution.
claims.statement: Cross-architecture determinism: a GSPL program expanded identically on two architectures produces byte-identical canonical outputs. Limited to architectures that implement the SplitMix64 + xoshiro256** + FNV-1a + Box-Muller stack without substitution.
claims.verificationMethod: Run an identical seed expansion on two architectures; assert hash match.

conditions: Types are encoded per RFC 8785 JCS exactly.
Top-level field ordering follows the GSPL convention.
falsificationCriteria: A NIST test vector fails
Two equivalent inputs produce different JCS canonical encodings
claims.scope: Within packages/canon-foundation. [Prompt 2: Prompt 2: Canonical serialization refined (Unicode NFKC, base64url, timestamp normalization). JCS + SHA-256 stack unchanged.]
claims.statement: GSPL canonical types (Genome, Assertion, Lineage, Authorization) emit JCS-canonical encoding of their structure and SHA-256 the encoding to a stable identifier.
claims.verificationMethod: NIST FIPS 180-4 vectors and RFC 8785 test vectors pinned in `src/canonicalize/jcs.test.ts`.

conditions: Inventions + sources + claims + architecture-decisions JSON exist
Tool can resolve references and detect orphans
Tool exits 0 on PASS, 2 on FAIL
falsificationCriteria: A malformed invention ID is accepted
Orphan inventions pass undetected
Report is non-deterministic across reruns
claims.scope: Within packages/provenance-checker and the bootstrap pipeline.
claims.statement: The provenance checker has validated the actual canonical registries (inventions.json, sources.json, claims.json, architecture-decisions.json) end-to-end and produced a deterministic validation report. Status is IMPLEMENTED only after this end-to-end execution succeeds.
claims.verificationMethod: Run `npm run check:provenance` and inspect the report; assert zero errors.

conditions: Seed uses canonical combinator gene types
A canonical architecture target is provided
No third-party architecture override is in effect
falsificationCriteria: A synthesized architecture lacks the structural requirements of the target
Test preservation rate across synthesis drops below documented threshold
claims.scope: Architecture synthesis from arbitrary seed input across the 26 domains; the per-type combinator layer is design-correct but end-to-end unverified. [Prompt 2: Prompt 2: Architecture synthesis supported through target contracts and reference fixtures. Gene combinator types (graph, topology, struct) provide the representation substrate.]
claims.statement: Architecture synthesis through the `struct`, `graph`, `topology`, and `field` gene types is a DESIGN CAPABILITY of the gene inventory. Robust end-to-end architecture synthesis is not yet proven; current implementation is a prototype.
claims.verificationMethod: A canonical synthesis test (Prompt 4) takes a seed and synthesizes a target architecture; asserts structural integrity and per-type operator satisfaction.

conditions: Tests are written in canonical AST or higher
Compile and interpret targets are within the canon
No external IO is performed during the test
falsificationCriteria: A round-tripped test produces different output than the canonical version
Test pass count changes after round-tripping
claims.scope: Within gene-types property suite and determinism tests; broader coverage is pending.
claims.statement: Test suites round-trip through compilation: tests written canonically survive AST interpretation, codegen, and re-interpretation with output equivalent to the canonical form. Currently PARTIALLY_IMPLEMENTED: round-tripping is verified for the gene-types property suite but not for arbitrary hand-written tests.
claims.verificationMethod: Run the canonical tests and the canonical-compiled equivalents; assert pass counts and output equivalence.

conditions: Same build inputs (seed, knowledge version)
Same canon-foundation determinism stack
No wall-clock-dependent inputs
falsificationCriteria: Two repeatable builds produce different artifacts
A wall-clock input leaks into the canonical encoding
claims.scope: Within the canon-foundation determinism stack. Cross-architecture coverage is RESEARCH_REQUIRED in GSPL-CLAIM-0007. [Prompt 2: Prompt 2: Deterministic entropy channels with golden vectors verified. Order-independent forks ensure cross-process reproducibility. 63 entropy tests pass.]
claims.statement: Independently repeated builds of the same seed produce byte-identical canonical gseed content. The canon-foundation determinism stack supports this for in-process runs; cross-host reproducibility (e.g. Windows + Linux) is PROTOTYPED via the deterministic RNG stack but full coverage tests are pending.
claims.verificationMethod: Run `npm run build` twice; assert byte-identical artifacts.
